title: Clock times are real times, not defaults
why: When one minute takes a large share of a stream's samples, it looks like a convention and not a time. Time-of-day can't then be used as an input. Why this happens is unconfirmed.
action: Ask the publisher what these stamps mean, and leave time-of-day out for the streams affected.
Rule Threshold Text: Fails above 5%. Needs review above 1%. Illustrative.
Rule Effect Text: Share of all samples that look like they were taken at the stated minute, if every clock time is believed, against if stamped times are set aside: 86.17 worked out carefully, 100 carelessly (%). That moves it by +16.1%.
Rule Test Text: Caught at the last check: its count rose from 5,526 to 10,902 when its own defect was planted in a private copy.
